newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban says UNHCR passed military information.
newsitem.headline: Taleban says UNHCR passed military information.

text.p: A senior member of the Taleban administration in Kabul was reported on Sunday to have accused employees of the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR of passing military information to the opposition.

An English-language report from the Taleban-controlled Bakhtar Information Agency said the Taleban, who hold Kabul, had "evidence that some of the UNHCR and several other institutions use UNHCR facilites against the Islamic State.
"For example through the wire-less system of the UNHCR they establish contact with the centres of opposition to the Islamic state and provide them with military information."
Bakhtar's reports are distributed to journalists and other foreign organisations by the Foreign Ministry.

Sunday's report described a meeting between the Taleban's acting deputy foreign minster, Shir Mohammed Abbas Stanakzai, and the deputy head of the United Nations Special Mission to Afghanistan, Francis Okelo.
It said Stanakzai also accused other, unnamed, foreign institutions of carrying weapons into Kabul.

"Some vehicles, carrying flags of some foreign institutions, were clandestinely carrying arms to Kabul for conducting subversive activites in the capital. (They) were arrested by the law enforcing authorites here." the report said.
The UNCHR put on hold most of its activites in Kabul after its female staff were refused permission to work by the purist Islamic Teleban and four of its male staff were arrested.
A UNHCR spokesman in the Pakistani capital of Islamabad recently described the staff as "petrified".
The UNHCR has requested the release of its arrested staffers.
The Bakhtar report said that some local associates of foreign institutions "were arrested and investigated about their unpatriotic acts."

The report continued: "In support of such anti-state elements the UNHCR asks us to let them free. This request is in full contradiction with the neutrality of the UN and other foreign charity organisations' principles and brings the UN neutrality under question."
